walkthroughs.body_html:
Geographical Investigations: UK Challenges — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Geographical Investigations: UK Challenges brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Geographical Investigations: UK Challenges.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why do earthquakes typically cause more deaths in LICs than HICs?
options: LICs often have poorly enforced building codes, weak emergency response, dense informal housing and limited preparedness — not because the earthquakes are stronger.
Earthquakes are caused by the Earth's core overheating.
LICs have more earthquake deaths because more earthquakes happen there.
HICs never have earthquake deaths because of advanced technology.

mcqs.q: What are the four pillars of food security?
options: Availability (enough food exists), access (people can obtain it), utilisation (nutritional quality and absorption) and stability (consistent over time) — defined by the FAO.
Food security just means producing enough food.
Earthquakes are caused by the Earth's core overheating.
Food security means storing food for emergencies.
